sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in Salina, KS?
sections.html:
Salina is the Saline County seat in north central Kansas, a regional hub for farm equipment, food manufacturing and health care. The 2020 census counted 46,889 people, and the Census Bureau estimate for July 1, 2025 is 46,094.

Sellers here deal with a few conditions that shape any sale: a river and levee system that came out of a major flood, severe thunderstorm and tornado history, and a county tax calendar that stays the same from year to year. The sections below cover each, along with the paperwork that closes a sale.

sections.h2: Where is Salina and how do you get there?
sections.html:
Salina sits where Interstate 70 meets Interstate 135, at an elevation of 1,224 feet in the Smoky Hills region. It is 81 miles north of Wichita, 164 miles west of Kansas City, Missouri, and 401 miles east of Denver.

The Smoky Hill River runs through the eastern part of the city and the Saline River flows just north. Mulberry Creek and Dry Creek cross the north and west. The city covers about 25 square miles. I-135 and US-81 run along the west side, I-70 and US-40 run along the north, and Ninth Street is the main north to south street, becoming K-143 north of I-70.

  • CityGo is the local bus service, with five routes.
  • Salina Municipal Airport has United Express flights to Chicago O'Hare, Houston and Denver.
  • Union Pacific runs one freight line through the north of the city.
  • The nearest Amtrak stop is in Newton.

Settlers from Lawrence founded the Salina Town Company in 1858 and named the town for the salty Saline River. The county was organized around it, and Salina incorporated as a city in 1870.

As the westernmost town on the Smoky Hill Trail, Salina grew as a trading post for emigrants, gold prospectors headed to Pikes Peak and area tribes. A second boom came in the 1940s and 1950s when the Smoky Hill Army Airfield was built. Lee Jeans opened its first garment factory in Salina in 1889.

sections.h2: What did the 1951 flood change in Salina?
sections.html:
In 1951 Salina experienced what the Army Corps of Engineers calls a 500-year flood. Afterward a federal levee system was built, and it cut off 6.8 miles of the Smoky Hill River's channel through downtown.

That old channel now receives runoff from a 4.6 square mile urban drainage rather than the 8,341 square miles it drained before. The city approved a Smoky Hill River Master Plan in 2010, and the Corps' restoration study lists design work from September 2026 to 2028, construction starting in 2028 and completion in 2030. If your house is near the river or the old channel, ask for the flood zone and any insurance history before setting a price.

sections.h2: What should Salina sellers know about tornadoes and hail?
sections.html:
Salina sits in a region prone to severe thunderstorms with damaging winds, hail and tornadoes. An F3 tornado struck the south part of the city on June 21, 1969, severely damaging or destroying more than 100 homes and businesses and injuring 60 people. Another F3 on September 25, 1973 passed through the southeast and destroyed two houses and a trailer park, and an EF3 passed the south side on June 11, 2008.

The climate numbers explain the wear on a house: the temperature reaches 90 degrees about 68 days a year and 100 degrees about 16 days, falls below freezing about 115 days, and the city gets about 32 inches of precipitation and 16.6 inches of snow. Roofs and siding here take real wear. If you have unrepaired storm damage, an as-is sale avoids a repair project.

Salina Regional Health Center is the largest employer in Saline County at 2,800 employees, according to a Salina Journal list drawn from the Salina Economic Development Organization. The hospital's own community page also names Schwan's Global Supply, described as the world's largest maker of frozen pizza, along with Exide Technology and Great Plains Manufacturing.

Manufacturing, education, health and social services lead the local economy, and agricultural transportation is a significant industry. The 7,000-seat Tony's Pizza Events Center hosts events. Kansas State University Polytechnic Campus, Kansas Wesleyan University and Salina Area Technical College are all located in the city.

sections.h2: Which schools and utilities serve a Salina house?
sections.html:
Salina USD 305 serves nearly all of the city and runs two high schools, Salina Central and Salina South, along with two middle schools and eight elementary schools. Small southeastern, southwestern areas fall into Southeast of Saline USD 306 and Ell-Saline USD 307, so confirm the district for your parcel.

The city's Department of Public Works handles water treatment and distribution, wastewater, sewer maintenance and trash collection, and Kansas Gas Service supplies natural gas. Arrange final billing with the city before you hand over the keys.

sections.h2: How do Saline County property taxes work for a seller?
sections.html:
Saline County lets owners pay real estate tax in full or in half by December 20. Unpaid first-half tax accrues interest from December 21, and the second half is due by May 10 of the following year.

Kansas sets the calendar for every county: valuation notices go out by March 1, appeals begin with a 30 day window after mailing, and tax statements are due out by December 1 under K.S.A. 79-2001. Ask your closing agent to prorate the current bill, and keep your valuation notice if you plan to contest the value before the sale.

sections.h2: What paperwork records a Salina sale?
sections.html:
A deed is recorded at the Saline County Register of Deeds, and under K.S.A. 79-1437c it must come with a completed sales validation questionnaire unless an exemption is clearly stated on the deed. The register keeps the questionnaire for five years and then destroys it.

Salina's property maintenance code sits in chapter 31 of its code of ordinances. If the house has a violation notice, deal with it before closing so the buyer does not inherit it.

sections.h2: Is a cash sale right for a Salina house?
sections.html: A cash sale suits homes that need roof or storm repairs, estate properties, houses with tenants, and sellers working to a date. Listing may bring more buyers when a house is in good repair. Contact us with the address and we will give you an honest comparison.

faqs.q: Is Salina, KS in a flood zone?
faqs.a: Some parts are near the Smoky Hill and Saline Rivers. The city had a 500-year flood in 1951, and a federal levee system followed, so check the flood zone for your parcel and ask about flood insurance before you price the house.

faqs.q: When are Saline County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Real estate tax can be paid in half or in full by December 20, with the second half due by May 10 of the following year. Unpaid first-half tax accrues interest beginning December 21.

faqs.q: What school district is Salina in?
faqs.a: Most of the city is in Salina USD 305. Small areas fall in Southeast of Saline USD 306, Ell-Saline USD 307 and Smoky Valley USD 400, so check your address.

faqs.q: Can I sell a storm-damaged Salina house as is?
faqs.a: Yes. Salina has a history of tornado and hail damage, and many owners prefer an as-is sale to a repair project. The offer will reflect the repairs the buyer takes on.

faqs.q: What does the sales validation questionnaire do?
faqs.a: It collects the sale price and sale conditions for the state valuation system and must accompany a deed unless the transfer is exempt. The register of deeds keeps it for five years.

faqs.q: Where do I find Salina's property maintenance rules?
faqs.a: They are in chapter 31 of the Salina Code of Ordinances, which is available on the city's Municode page.
